title: feat(trigger-api)!: the inbound hook door refuses the body-only signature form, so only the timestamped form verifies (ruling B on #22805, step 3)
body:
Fixes #22826
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

Step 3 of ruling B on #22805 (record `6108492902`, maintainer 「同意」), at the position triage set (`6108760218`): the trigger-api inbound hook door refuses a verdict whose `scheme` is `body-only`. Core's `verifyHttpSignature` keeps both forms, because it is the receiver half of the body-only form our own outbound senders sign.

## What changes

- **The door** (`packages/triggers/trigger-api/src/api-trigger.ts`). One private function, `verifyInboundSignature`, makes the door's signature judgement: core's verdict, then an exhaustive switch over the verified `scheme`. `v1` is accepted. `body-only` is refused as `signature-body-only`. `handleRequest` and the exported `verifySignature` both call it, so the export answers what the door answers. The refusal runs right after verification, before the JSON parse and the enqueue, through the existing `refuseUnverified`. So a body-only post gets the uniform `401 INVALID_SIGNATURE` built by PR #22822, and nothing is enqueued, even when the value is the secret's HMAC of the body.
- **The deprecation line is gone**, with `bodyOnlyDeprecationLogged` and its initialiser.
- **The cause vocabulary gains exactly one entry**, `signature-body-only`, in the same voice as `signature-outside-window`. The `signature-malformed` text no longer says "neither accepted form", because one form is accepted now.
- **Describe-only text:**
  - the `ITriggerApiService.handleInboundHook` docblock (`packages/spec`) names the timestamped form as the only one accepted and the body-only form as refused. This is the relay `6108557878` on #6017. The type is unchanged.
  - the plugin docblock and the route-ledger note say the same.
- **Changeset** `.changeset/22826-refuse-body-only-signature.md`. `@objectstack/trigger-api` is `major`: a breaking narrowing on the v18 line in `next` pre mode, the grade 22502/22565/22572 used. `@objectstack/spec` is `patch`: the docblock reaches `dist/contracts/index.d.ts`. The changeset has the BREAKING banner and FROM → TO. Its ADR-0087 disposition is `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: no metadata moves, and what narrows is a value a third-party sender computes.

⛔ Not touched: `packages/core` (`verifyHttpSignature`, `signHttpBody`), the outbound senders, `webhooks.mdx` §6, ADR-0138 (its D7 sentence waits for that ADR's next revision, per the ruling), `content/docs/releases/`.

## Pins beside the door (done-when, one by one)

| done-when | pin |
| --- | --- |
| body-only, valid for the secret, is refused with the uniform 401, nothing enqueued | `api-trigger.test.ts` "refuses a body-only signature that IS the secret's HMAC of the body". It first asserts core verifies the value as `{ valid: true, scheme: 'body-only' }`, so the refusal is the door's policy and not a broken fixture. It then asserts the full envelope, an empty queue, no flow run, and exactly one `warn` per post, which is the refusal with cause `signature-body-only`. |
| the same, in the uniform table (the cause log line) | two new `SIGNED_BUT_UNVERIFIED` rows, under the default hook id and a custom one. They feed "every unverified post gets the same status and the same envelope" and "the server log records the real cause of each refusal". |
| the same, hosted shape and parity | `inbound-hook-member.test.ts`: the arm-table row `202` becomes `401 INVALID_SIGNATURE`, published false. The member/mount parity table compares the same row. |
| CONTROL: timestamped inside the window accepted | "CONTROL: accepts a fresh timestamped post", plus the window-edge test. |
| CONTROL: outside the window refused | "CONTROL: refuses a replay outside the window", plus "CONTROL: refuses a stale timestamp the HMAC genuinely covers". |
| CONTROL: outbound `signHttpBody` output unchanged | new "CONTROL: the outbound form is unchanged". Core's `signHttpBody` still writes the body-only value byte-for-byte as the published recipe, and core still verifies it. |
| the deprecation warning is gone | the "exactly one `warn` per post" assertion above (ablation C below). |
| `verifySignature` agrees with the door | both `verifySignature` tests assert `false` for the right secret's body-only value. |

## Ablation: every negative pin, red, then restored

Each mutation went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (wrap mode, anchor hit 1 → 0, blob changed) inside a wrapper that has its own `trap … EXIT INT TERM` restore. Each was restored with `git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH` and proven by blob equality with `HEAD:path` (`aff2541dd93b`) and an empty `git diff HEAD`. The trigger-api suites import `./api-trigger.js` / `./plugin.js` relatively, straight from source, so no build or `dist/` leg applies. The dogfood suite aliases `@objectstack/trigger-api` to source.

- **A: body-only accepted again** (`return { valid: true };` for `body-only`). **7 failed / 48 passed (55)**: both `verifySignature` tests ("expected true to be false"), the refusal test ("first post: expected { status: 202 … } to deeply equal { status: 401 … }"), both uniform-table tests ("the right secret, in the body-only form: expected { status: 202 … }" and "expected [] to deeply equal [ 'signature-body-only' ]"), the member arm table ("expected 202 to be 401"), and parity ("the mount's own answer: expected 202 to be 401"). Restored: OK.
- **B: cause mislabelled** (`signature-mismatch`). **2 failed / 53 passed**: "expected [ 'signature-mismatch' ] to deeply equal [ 'signature-body-only' ]" in the refusal test and the cause-log test. The envelope pins stay green, as they should. Restored: OK.
- **C: a deprecation `warn` put back beside the refusal.** **1 failed / 54 passed**: "expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 2 times". Restored: OK.
- **Reverse check on the real composition.** The dogfood credential-channel suite was run with its old body-only signer against the new door. **7 failed / 3 passed (10)**, each "expected 401 to be 202", through the real engine, the credential channel and the real `ApiTrigger`. Restored: OK. This is why the suite's signer flips (below).

## Whole-repo pin sweep

Grepped for the signature header, `sha256=`, `signHttpBody`, `verifyHttpSignature`, `INVALID_SIGNATURE`, the hook path and `ApiTrigger` across the repo.

- **Flipped:**
  - `api-trigger.test.ts`: the two "body-only still accepted" tests, the "both forms" control and the two `verifySignature` tests. Every valid post in the older describes now signs the timestamped form, and the duplicate local `sigV1` helpers became one file-level pair.
  - `inbound-hook-member.test.ts`: the body-only `202` row.
  - `packages/qa/dogfood/test/flow-credential-channel.dogfood.test.ts`: its signer was body-only against the real door, so every `202` it expects would be `401`; it now signs the timestamped form.
  - `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-hooks.test.ts`: the member double that "carries the trigger's verifier" now accepts `v1` only, as the door does, and its posts sign `v1`. It is outside the claim's declared surface; it is here because ruling B's sweep covers the whole repo, and the change is the double's fidelity, not a new pin.
- **Left verbatim, because they guard a still-illegal shape:** the `sha256=` value carried with a `t=` prefix (refused, no fallback), body-only under another secret (`signature-mismatch`), `sha256=zz`, and the `503` rows signed with a body-only value under a wrong secret.
- **Hand-written docs:** no sentence in `content/docs/**` (outside `releases/` and `references/`), the showcase, the QA checklist or the skill tells a sender the inbound door accepts the body-only form. #22825 had already rewritten them. Nothing to correct.

## Measured against the dispatch's mechanism assumptions

1. Holds. `verifyHttpSignature` returns `{ valid: true, scheme: 'v1' | 'body-only' }`, and `handleRequest` read it at the deprecation branch. No core change was needed.
2. Holds in kind, but the count is off by two. Before this PR the vocabulary had six causes (`unknown-flow`, `wrong-hook-id` and four `signature-*`). Adding exactly one makes seven, five of them `signature-*`. "The four-cause log line" is read as "the cause log line pins the new cause", and it does.
3. Holds. The arm-table and parity rows flipped in place.
4. Holds: there was nothing to correct (above).

## Verification at `78b92702d`

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/trigger-api exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 3 files, **55 passed**.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/trigger-api typecheck`: exit 0 (the tsconfig includes `src/**/*`, tests included).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/domains/automation-hooks.test.ts`: **19 passed**. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck`: exit 0, test layer held in its ledger.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 test/flow-credential-channel.dogfood.test.ts`: **10 passed**. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood typecheck`: exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/contracts/trigger-api-service.test.ts`: 1 passed. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck`: exit 0.
- Gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, re-derived on this change: 87 commands. That is a superset of the dispatch's 78; the nine extra ones are the changeset gates, `check:route-envelope` and two release self-tests. All 87 ran, plus `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` ("All 14 generated artifacts are up to date"), and every one exited 0. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: eight unrelated packages had no `dist/`). Those packages were restored from turbo's cache, and the re-run exited 0: "107 published require entry point(s) across 66 package(s) load". `dispatch-gates --ran`, given every command with its exit code: "87 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 87 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 87 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3)".

**Declared narrowing:** for `@objectstack/spec` the change is TSDoc text in one interface, so its full suite is declared to CI and only the contract's own test, the typecheck and the derived spec gates ran here. For `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/dogfood` only the edited test files ran, with each package's typecheck. Their full suites (the dogfood gate included) are CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- ADR-0041 line 119 still says "HMAC signature verification (GitHub/Stripe style)". GitHub's style is the body-only form. This is a governed surface, so it is noted and not edited; its natural carrier is ADR-0041's next revision, beside ADR-0138 D7's correction.
- `packages/core/src/security/http-signature.ts`'s docblock ("so the body-only form stays accepted; refusing it is a decision of its own, not this definition's") stays true: the decision is now taken, at the door.
- The contract-tier review of record (`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`) for the describe-only spec text and the breaking narrowing is the owning seat's, after this PR.
